Read a skill folder

Source: R/core-skill.R
hr_skill.Rd

hr_skill() reads a skill: a folder you chose that holds instructions for one step of a run. Give the skill to a step with hr_step(..., skill = s); inside hr_chain() the step's ctx$call() and ctx$call_json() then send the skill's instructions and references as a system message before the step's own messages, and ctx$skill holds the skill.

Usage

hr_skill(path)

Arguments

path

The skill's folder, one string.

Value

A list of class hr_skill with name, description and version (NULL when the header has none), instructions (one string), references (a named character vector of file texts, named by path under references/), scripts (a named character vector of full paths, named by path under scripts/), path (the folder's full path) and hash.

Details

The folder holds:

SKILL.md

Required. It starts with a header between two lines that are exactly ---. Each header line is key: value, with the value on the same line; matching quotes around it are removed. name is required, and description and version are kept. Any other key warns with class hr_skill_unknown_key and is ignored. A value that is indented, nested or spread over lines (| or >) is an error, since the header is read without a YAML parser. Everything after the closing --- is the instructions.

references/

Optional text files, added after the instructions. A file with a nul byte, or that is not UTF-8 text, is an error. Line endings are read as "\n", so a CRLF copy gives the same text and hash.

scripts/

Optional. The scripts are listed by path and never run. To run one, wrap it yourself in a command step, as in hr_step_command("lint", c(rscript, s$scripts[["check.R"]])).

The folder is read only where you point: the package never looks for skills, and a model never chooses one. A file that is a link to somewhere outside the folder is an error, and so are a broken link, a references/ or scripts/ folder that is a link to somewhere outside, a link to a folder under either of them, and a folder with more than 50 reference files, more than 50 scripts, or more than 200,000 bytes in all. These limits are fixed. All errors have class hr_bad_skill.

A skill's text goes into the prompt as it is, so a skill from someone else can carry instructions you did not mean to send (prompt injection). Read a skill before you use it.

The skill's hash covers the header, the instructions, each reference and every byte of each script, so editing any of them changes it. A step given a skill has the hash among its fixed settings and in its fingerprint, so a chain with a skill has a different configuration from the same chain without it, and a benchmark gets a param.<step>.skill column naming the skill and the start of its hash.

Examples

dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "units-skill")
dir.create(file.path(dir, "references"), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
writeLines(c("---", "name: units", "description: Give amounts with units.",
             "version: 1.0.0", "---",
             "Always state the unit and the currency of every amount."),
           file.path(dir, "SKILL.md"))
writeLines("Write million in full.", file.path(dir, "references", "style.md"))
s <- hr_skill(dir)
s
#> <hr_skill> units version 1.0.0 (1af7430e0b8c)
#>   Give amounts with units. 
#>   instructions: 55 characters
#>   references: style.md 

# In a chain, the step's requests carry the skill as a system message.
cl <- gr_mock_client(function(m, p) "45.2 million dollars")
ask <- hr_step("ask", function(input, ctx) ctx$call(input)$text, skill = s)
chain <- hr_chain(ask = ask, name = "with-skill")
chain$params
#> $ask.skill
#> [1] "units@1af7430e0b8c"
#> 
ref <- hr_reference(list(q1 = "What was revenue?"), labels = "45.2 million dollars",
                    cluster = "a", split = "test")
bench <- hr_benchmark(chain, ref, runs = 5, client = cl, scorer = hr_scorer_exact())
sent <- cl$calls()[[1]]$messages
vapply(sent, function(m) m$role, "")
#> [1] "system" "user"  
unique(bench$param.ask.skill)
#> [1] "units@1af7430e0b8c"
unlink(dir, recursive = TRUE)
